headline: Protein language models and generative models predict and design biomolecular properties
label: Learned Protein Property Prediction
summary: Recent preprints and papers pair pretrained protein and DNA language model features with task-specific heads, adapters, and generative models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of pretrained biomolecular representations. Protein language model embeddings supply features for antimicrobial peptide MIC prediction (STAMP), protein-protein binding affinity (BindPred), and phage protein classification with generative augmentation (EAGP). CodonMoE applies a lightweight codon-level mixture-of-experts adapter so a DNA language model can predict RNA properties without RNA pretraining. Generative work follows a related logic: AgentPLM couples a protein language model with tool-calling decoding (ESMFold, FoldX, AutoDock Vina) and trajectory-level preference optimisation for sequence design, GeoCoupling learns temporal couplings between sequence and structure in co-design, and DPDiff and MolPIF address ligand and molecule generation through interaction priors and parameter-space interpolation flows. The items are heterogeneous, so this shared thread describes the dominant pattern rather than a method common to every item. The distinguishing element is the explicit attachment of task-specific components, such as adapters, external tools, priors, or augmentation, to frozen or pretrained representations.
